title: Yosef ben Simai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Shabbat 121a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.121a.5) relates that Yosef was the king’s steward. When fire broke out in his courtyard on Shabbat, Tzippori’s garrison came to put it out. He would not let them, and by a miracle rain put out the fire. The parallels in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 16:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.16.7.2), [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 8:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.8.5.8) and [Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 4:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.4.9.2) call him Yose ben Simai. In [Yevamot 115a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.115a.11), two scholars traveled by ship with Abba Yose ben Simai. When it sank, Rabbi permitted their wives to remarry. Hyman considers that this might be Yosef ben Simai. He cites Abba (bar) Simi in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 15:5.[^1]

notes.text: The Bavli’s fire story names Yosef and says he need not have prevented the garrison from acting. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2002&lang=en) compares both episodes and reports Yosef/Yose readings in the legal compilations. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 15:5 did not furnish the reported Abba (bar) Simi form.
